reading.review:
Seven generations of the Buendía family rise and fall in the mythical town of Macondo, where the miraculous is narrated with the calm matter-of-factness of daily news. García Márquez's prose has an unmistakable musical cadence.

Keeping the family tree handy helps on a first read, though the recurring names are themselves part of the novel's hypnotic theme of cyclical time.

note.note-text: The famous opening sentence telescopes past, present, and future into a single breath.
The insomnia plague and labeling every object in town — a brilliant metaphor for memory and language.
